intervals.label: Phase-I construction
intervals.note: Anchored to the Phase-I Technical Design Report (December 2018), the earliest dated evidence of the Phase-I programme among the sources consulted, as an approximate lower bound -- not a stated 'construction began' date. The collaboration's site (comet.kek.jp, checked 2026-10-25) gives as its latest dated activity the CM48 collaboration meeting of 27-31 July 2026, which shows the programme is still ongoing; the site makes no statement that data taking or commissioning has been completed.
intervals.quote: The Technical Design for the COMET Phase-I experiment is presented in this paper.

key_specs.label: Phase-I sensitivity goal (90% C.L. upper limit)

quantity.note: The TDR states both a design sensitivity (3.1×10⁻¹⁵) and the corresponding 90% C.L. upper limit if no signal is seen (7×10⁻¹⁵); the upper-limit figure is recorded as the primary quantity with the design sensitivity in the note, both from the same quote.
quantity.quote: The experimental sensitivity goal for this process in the Phase-I experiment is 3.1x10^-15, or 90 % upper limit of branching ratio of 7x10^-15, which is a factor of 100 improvement over the existing limit.
the 3.2 kW 8 GeV proton beam from J-PARC will be used.

name: COMET
notes: No physics result is listed on the collaboration's site (comet.kek.jp, checked 2026-10-25). The Phase-I Technical Design Report (December 2018) describes a staged programme (Phase-I, then Phase-II) and the site shows continuing activity (latest dated entry: the CM48 collaboration meeting of 27-31 July 2026); neither reports data taking or a first physics result.

The coordinate of the J-PARC Hadron Hall site record (site:j-parc-hadron-hall) is approximate: the centroid of an OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a surveyed position of the COMET hall (see that record's own notes).

physics_goals.quote: COMET is an experiment at J-PARC, Japan, which will search for neutrinoless conversion of muons into electrons in the field of an aluminium nucleus (mu-e conversion, mu- N -> e- N); a lepton flavor violating process.
physics_goals.value: Search for neutrinoless muon-to-electron conversion in the field of an aluminium nucleus (μ⁻ N → e⁻ N), a charged-lepton-flavor-violating process, in a staged Phase-I then Phase-II programme

summary.plain: An experiment being built at the J-PARC laboratory in Japan to look for a muon turning directly into an electron near an aluminium atom -- a process the Standard Model forbids. It is being built in stages, starting with a smaller first phase.
summary.technical: COMET (J-PARC Hadron Experimental Facility): stages a search for μ⁻ N → e⁻ N conversion, using curved-solenoid muon transport from an 8 GeV, 3.2 kW proton beam off the J-PARC Main Ring. Phase-I targets a 90% C.L. branching-ratio upper limit of 7×10⁻¹⁵ (design sensitivity 3.1×10⁻¹⁵) using CyDet, a factor of 100 improvement over the previous (SINDRUM II) limit; StrECAL measures background in view of Phase-II. Collaboration: more than 290 researchers from 48 institutes. No physics result is listed on the collaboration's site as of 2026-10-25 (its latest dated entry is the CM48 meeting of 27-31 July 2026).

unique_capabilities.quote: Two types of detectors, CyDet and StrECAL, will be used for detecting the mu-e conversion events, and for measuring the beam-related background events in view of the Phase-II experiment, respectively.
unique_capabilities.value: Uses a curved-solenoid pion/muon transport system (to select low-momentum muons and suppress backgrounds) feeding cylindrical or straw-tube/electromagnetic-calorimeter detector systems (CyDet for Phase-I; StrECAL for background measurement toward Phase-II)
